symptoms: Olive-green to dark lesions on leaves and fruit; lesions may become corky and fruit may crack.
favorable_conditions: Cool, wet periods and prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Use resistant cultivars; remove or accelerate decomposition of fallen leaves; maintain an open canopy.
management: Sanitation and canopy management; monitor infection periods.
organic_management: Leaf sanitation, resistant cultivars, pruning and canopy drying.
chemical_management: Use only locally registered fungicides and follow the current crop label.

symptoms: Brown or purple leaf spots, limb cankers and black, rotting fruit.
favorable_conditions: Warm, humid conditions; dead wood and mummified fruit can provide inoculum.
prevention: Remove mummified fruit and dead/cankered wood; prune for airflow.
management: Sanitation, pruning and removal of infected plant material.
organic_management: Remove infected material and maintain orchard hygiene.
chemical_management: Use locally registered products according to the apple disease label and extension guidance.

symptoms: Yellow-orange leaf spots; fruit infections may form abnormal growths.
favorable_conditions: Moist spring weather; requires compatible cedar/juniper and apple-family hosts.
prevention: Choose resistant cultivars and reduce nearby alternate hosts where practical.
management: Prune infected tissue and use resistant varieties; fungicide timing is preventive when needed.
organic_management: Resistant varieties, pruning and sanitation.
chemical_management: Chemical control must follow local registration and label directions.

symptoms: White powdery growth on leaves and shoots; distorted or weakened young tissue.
favorable_conditions: Warm conditions with humid air but relatively dry leaf surfaces.
prevention: Improve airflow, avoid excessive nitrogen, remove heavily affected tissue where feasible.
management: Canopy management and timely disease monitoring.
organic_management: Sanitation and airflow management.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides according to the crop label.

disease: Cercospora leaf spot / Gray leaf spot
pathogen_or_cause: Cercospora zeae-maydis and related Cercospora spp.
symptoms: Rectangular gray-to-tan lesions that develop between leaf veins.
favorable_conditions: Warm, humid weather and extended leaf wetness.
prevention: Use resistant hybrids, crop rotation and residue management.
management: Scout lower leaves and manage susceptible fields using integrated disease management.
organic_management: Rotation, residue management and resistant hybrids.
chemical_management: Use only locally registered products and follow label/extension timing.

symptoms: Small reddish-brown pustules on leaves that release rust-colored spores.
favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures and humid conditions.
prevention: Use resistant hybrids where available and monitor fields.
management: Scout and manage severe susceptible crops according to local recommendations.
organic_management: Resistant hybrids and field monitoring.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides only when justified by local recommendations.

symptoms: Long, gray-green to tan cigar-shaped lesions on leaves.
favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures with frequent moisture and humid conditions.
prevention: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops and manage residue where appropriate.
management: Early scouting and integrated management are important in susceptible fields.
organic_management: Rotation, resistant hybrids and residue management.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides when recommended.

symptoms: Circular brown leaf lesions and dark, shriveled fruit that become mummified.
favorable_conditions: Warm, humid weather with repeated rainfall.
prevention: Remove mummified fruit and infected tissue; maintain canopy airflow.
management: Sanitation, pruning and timely disease monitoring.
organic_management: Removal of mummies and infected tissue.
chemical_management: Use locally registered grape fungicides according to label and extension guidance.

symptoms: Leaf striping or spotting, berry spotting and internal wood discoloration; symptoms can vary.
favorable_conditions: Stress and infection through pruning wounds are associated with disease development.
prevention: Use clean planting material and minimize large pruning wounds; remove severely affected vines.
management: Sanitation, pruning-wound management and removal of severely affected vines.
organic_management: Clean propagation material and careful pruning hygiene.
chemical_management: Follow locally registered recommendations; chemical control is limited for established wood disease.

symptoms: Leaf spots that may enlarge and cause premature leaf yellowing or defoliation.
favorable_conditions: Warm, humid conditions and prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Improve canopy airflow and remove infected plant debris.
management: Integrated sanitation and canopy management.
organic_management: Sanitation and airflow management.
chemical_management: Use locally registered products only when recommended for grape leaf diseases.

pathogen_or_cause: Candidatus Liberibacter spp.; transmitted by citrus psyllids
symptoms: Blotchy leaf mottling, yellow shoots, small or misshapen fruit and decline.
favorable_conditions: Presence of infected trees and psyllid vectors; disease spreads through infected propagation material.
prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material, monitor/control vectors and remove infected trees where mandated.
management: Integrated vector and infected-tree management.
organic_management: Healthy planting material and vector exclusion/management.
chemical_management: Follow official local citrus-health and pesticide regulations.

symptoms: Small water-soaked or dark lesions on leaves and fruit; fruit spots can crack or become sunken.
favorable_conditions: Warm, wet weather and frequent rain.
prevention: Use tolerant/resistant cultivars where available and maintain good orchard hygiene.
management: Canopy management, sanitation and disease monitoring.
organic_management: Pruning for airflow and removal of severely affected tissue.
chemical_management: Use only products registered for peach bacterial diseases in the country of use.

symptoms: Water-soaked or dark leaf spots, defoliation and raised or scabby fruit lesions.
favorable_conditions: Warm, wet conditions and splash dispersal.
prevention: Use clean seed/transplants, resistant varieties where available, avoid overhead irrigation and rotate crops.
management: Sanitation and integrated disease management.
organic_management: Clean seed, crop rotation and drip irrigation.
chemical_management: Use locally registered bactericides according to label.

symptoms: Dark circular leaf lesions often with concentric rings; older leaves are affected first.
favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures, leaf wetness and plant stress.
prevention: Use healthy seed, crop rotation, balanced nutrition and remove volunteer hosts.
management: Scout early and maintain plant vigor and sanitation.
organic_management: Rotation, sanitation and balanced nutrition.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides when needed.

symptoms: Water-soaked irregular leaf lesions that rapidly turn brown; white sporulation may occur under humid conditions.
favorable_conditions: Cool to mild temperatures, high humidity and leaf wetness.
prevention: Use certified seed, resistant/tolerant varieties where available, destroy volunteers and scout frequently.
management: Rapid sanitation and timely integrated management are critical.
organic_management: Resistant varieties, sanitation and careful irrigation.
chemical_management: Use locally registered late-blight products according to local forecasting/label guidance.

symptoms: White powdery colonies on leaf surfaces followed by yellowing and premature senescence.
favorable_conditions: Warm conditions with humid air; disease can develop without free water on leaves.
prevention: Use resistant varieties, good spacing and airflow; avoid excessive nitrogen.
management: Monitor early and manage infected foliage/canopy density.
organic_management: Resistant varieties and canopy airflow.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides according to label.

symptoms: Small dark purple to reddish leaf spots that can enlarge and give leaves a scorched appearance.
favorable_conditions: Warm, wet weather and prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Use resistant/tolerant cultivars, remove infected debris and improve airflow.
management: Sanitation and canopy management.
organic_management: Remove diseased leaves and reduce leaf wetness.
chemical_management: Use locally registered strawberry fungicides when recommended.

symptoms: Small dark leaf spots, defoliation and raised dark lesions on fruit.
favorable_conditions: Warm, wet conditions; splash and contaminated seed/transplants spread bacteria.
prevention: Use clean seed/transplants, resistant varieties where available, avoid overhead irrigation and rotate crops.
management: Sanitation, crop rotation and careful irrigation.
organic_management: Clean seed and sanitation.
chemical_management: Use only locally registered products according to the tomato label.

symptoms: Brown leaf lesions with concentric rings, often beginning on older foliage; can cause defoliation.
favorable_conditions: Warm, humid conditions and leaf wetness.
prevention: Crop rotation, sanitation, mulch and good airflow.
management: Scout early, maintain plant vigor and reduce soil splash.
organic_management: Mulching, sanitation and crop rotation.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides when needed.

symptoms: Rapidly expanding water-soaked green-gray to brown lesions; white sporulation may appear under humid conditions.
favorable_conditions: Cool to mild temperatures, high humidity and prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, healthy transplants and rapid removal of infected material.
management: Frequent scouting and integrated management are important.
organic_management: Sanitation and resistant varieties.
chemical_management: Use locally registered late-blight products according to label and local forecasts.

symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces with olive-green to brown velvety growth underneath.
favorable_conditions: High relative humidity and poor air circulation.
prevention: Improve ventilation/spacing, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and use resistant varieties.
management: Remove heavily affected leaves and manage greenhouse humidity.
organic_management: Airflow, sanitation and resistant varieties.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides when recommended.

symptoms: Numerous small circular leaf spots with dark margins and pale centers; lower leaves usually affected first.
favorable_conditions: Warm, wet conditions and splash dispersal.
prevention: Remove infected debris, mulch soil, rotate crops and avoid overhead irrigation.
management: Sanitation and reduction of leaf wetness.
organic_management: Mulching, rotation and sanitation.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides when necessary.

symptoms: Fine stippling or bronzing, webbing and leaf drying under severe infestation.
favorable_conditions: Hot, dry conditions; dusty conditions and broad-spectrum pesticide disruption of natural enemies can contribute.
prevention: Reduce plant stress, conserve natural enemies and monitor leaf undersides.
management: Integrated pest management and early monitoring.
organic_management: Water management, biological control and removal of heavily infested tissue where practical.
chemical_management: Use only registered miticides when thresholds justify treatment; follow label.

symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots that may have concentric rings; fruit can develop sunken lesions.
favorable_conditions: Warm, humid weather and prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Use clean transplants, improve airflow and reduce leaf wetness.
management: Scout and manage canopy humidity and sanitation.
organic_management: Sanitation and airflow.
chemical_management: Use locally registered fungicides according to label.

pathogen_or_cause: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus; transmitted mainly by whiteflies
symptoms: Upward leaf curling, yellowing, stunting and reduced fruit set.
favorable_conditions: High whitefly pressure and infected plants/propagation material.
prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, clean transplants and manage whiteflies.
management: Rogue infected plants where appropriate and use integrated vector management.
organic_management: Resistant varieties, exclusion and biological control of vectors.
chemical_management: Use only locally registered whitefly-management products and follow resistance-management guidance.

symptoms: Mottled light/dark green leaves, distortion and variable fruit symptoms; plants may be stunted.
favorable_conditions: Virus carried on contaminated seed, tools, hands and plant debris.
prevention: Use certified seed, sanitation and resistant varieties; avoid handling plants when wet.
management: Remove infected plants and disinfect tools and hands.
organic_management: Sanitation and resistant varieties.
chemical_management: No curative chemical treatment; manage vectors/handling pathways and infected material.
